title: ONG-OT vulnerability prioritization: dataset, method, and sector-specific validation (extended version of the TPEC 2027 paper)
description:
Reproducibility package for an extended, journal-length analysis of CISA Industrial Control Systems (ICS) advisories relevant to oil and gas pipeline operators, prepared as an extension of a conference paper for submission to IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics.

This package reuses an already-verified, deduplicated dataset of 13,939 CVE–advisory pairs (2010–2026) and adds four new contributions: (1) an EPSS-threshold sensitivity analysis showing how much of the study's exploitation-response flag rate depends on an author-chosen parameter; (2) a statistically tested stratification of the pipeline-relevant subset by classification-confidence tier (Mann-Whitney U, tier1 n=42 vs. tier2 n=3,692); (3) a year-over-year trend regression on the pipeline-relevant share of advisories, 2010–2025; and (4) an explicit, citable coverage-and-provenance crosswalk of TSA Pipeline-2021-02 outcome groups against five independently published control frameworks (NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, IEC 62443, CIS Controls v8, and NIST CSF 2.0), replacing an unsubstantiated claim of “operator validation” with a transparent public-standards proxy and disclosing exactly what share of that crosswalk (40%) rests on the authors' own judgment versus a framework's own primary text.

Contents: new analysis code (src/), configuration and taxonomy files, documentation including a full author-verification checklist (docs/), figures, and the final, signed-off manuscript (manuscript/). Every number in the manuscript is traced to a machine-written stats.json file produced by a documented, versioned pipeline — nothing is asserted without a reproducible source. No primary operator data (interviews or surveys) was collected for this study; this is disclosed explicitly in the manuscript itself, not only in a limitations section.
